scope: Numbers 31–36, all 228 public verses. Prior revisions remain unchanged.

source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public Numbers 31–36 align directly with all 228 corresponding Hebrew records. Each original XML record is hashed in full. Earlier Numbers numbering differences and the two-record binding at public 26:1 remain preserved in earlier ledgers.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Retains the divine speech formula opening the command.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD spoke to Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves Israel’s vengeance and the death idiom without replacing either with an explanation.
verses.before: “Take vengeance for the Israelites against the Midianites. Afterward you will be gathered to your people.”
verses.after: “Take vengeance on the Midianites for the Israelites. Afterward you will be gathered to your people.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Take vengeance for the Israelites against the Midianites. Afterward you shall be gathered to your people.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the shift from Israel’s vengeance to the LORD’s vengeance in Moses’ address.
verses.before: Moses spoke to the people, saying, “Arm men from among you for war, so that they may go against Midian to execute the LORD’s vengeance on Midian.
verses.after: Moses told the people, “Arm some of your men for war. They are to attack Midian and carry out the LORD’s vengeance against it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses spoke to the people, saying, “Arm men from among you for war, so that they may go against Midian to execute the LORD’s vengeance on Midian.

verses.rationale: Retains the emphatic repetition of a thousand per tribe.
verses.before: You will send one thousand from each tribe, from all the tribes of Israel, to the war.”
verses.after: Send a thousand from each tribe—a thousand from every tribe of Israel—to the war.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall send one thousand from each tribe, from all the tribes of Israel, to the war.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the tribal levy and its explicit total.
verses.before: So from the thousands of Israel there were supplied one thousand from each tribe, twelve thousand armed for war.
verses.after: So a thousand men from each tribe were supplied from Israel’s thousands: twelve thousand armed for war.
verses.tsw_comparator: So from the thousands of Israel there were supplied one thousand from each tribe, twelve thousand armed for war.

verses.rationale: Identifies Phinehas clearly but does not specify unmentioned holy articles.
verses.before: Moses sent them to the war, one thousand from each tribe, along with Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest, with the holy vessels and the trumpets for the signal in his hand.
verses.after: Moses sent them to war, a thousand from each tribe, along with Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest. Phinehas carried the holy articles and the trumpets for sounding the signal.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses sent them to the war, one thousand from each tribe, along with Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest, with the holy vessels and the trumpets for the signal in his hand.

verses.rationale: Retains the unrestricted male terminology within this battle report rather than narrowing it to soldiers.
verses.before: They fought against Midian, as the LORD commanded Moses, and killed every male.
verses.after: They made war on Midian as the LORD had commanded Moses, and they killed every male.
verses.tsw_comparator: They fought against Midian, as the LORD commanded Moses, and killed every male.

verses.rationale: Preserves all five royal names and Balaam’s separate identification.
verses.before: They killed the kings of Midian along with the rest of those slain: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, the five kings of Midian. They also killed Balaam son of Beor with the sword.
verses.after: Among those they killed were the five kings of Midian: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur and Reba. They also killed Balaam son of Beor with the sword.
verses.tsw_comparator: They killed the kings of Midian along with the rest of those slain: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, the five kings of Midian. They also killed Balaam son of Beor with the sword.

verses.rationale: Makes captivity explicit and keeps children within the captured population.
verses.before: The Israelites took captive the women of Midian and their little ones, and they took as plunder all their cattle, flocks, and goods.
verses.after: The Israelites captured the women and little children of Midian. They took all their cattle, flocks and wealth as plunder.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Israelites took captive the women of Midian and their little ones, and they took as plunder all their cattle, flocks, and goods.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes settled towns from encampments while retaining the repeated totality.
verses.before: They burned with fire all the cities where they lived and all their encampments.
verses.after: They burned all the towns where the Midianites lived and all their encampments.
verses.tsw_comparator: They burned with fire all the cities where they lived and all their encampments.

verses.rationale: Keeps human and animal captives together in the accounting language.
verses.before: They took all the spoil and all the plunder, both people and animals,
verses.after: They took all the plunder and all the captives, both people and animals.
verses.tsw_comparator: They took all the spoil and all the plunder, both people and animals,

verses.rationale: Unfolds the long destination clause without losing the three recipients or location.
verses.before: and brought the captives, plunder, and spoil to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the congregation of the Israelites, to the camp in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho.
verses.after: They brought the captives, the captured goods and the plunder to Moses, Eleazar the priest and the Israelite community, at the camp on the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho.
verses.tsw_comparator: and brought the captives, plunder, and spoil to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the congregation of the Israelites, to the camp in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho.

verses.rationale: Preserves the outside-camp setting that anticipates purification.
verses.before: Moses, Eleazar the priest, and all the leaders of the congregation went out to meet them outside the camp.
verses.after: Moses, Eleazar the priest and all the community’s leaders went outside the camp to meet them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses, Eleazar the priest, and all the leaders of the congregation went out to meet them outside the camp.

verses.rationale: Identifies the officers by both ranks and the cause of their presence.
verses.before: Moses became angry with the officers of the army, the commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds who had come from the service of war.
verses.after: Moses was angry with the army’s officers, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds who had returned from the campaign.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses became angry with the officers of the army, the commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds who had come from the service of war.

verses.rationale: Preserves Moses’ accusatory question and its broad category rather than softening the demand.
verses.before: Moses said to them, “Have you kept all the women alive?
verses.after: “Have you kept all the females alive?” he asked them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses said to them, “Have you kept all the women alive?

verses.rationale: Attributes the accusation and Balaam connection to Moses’ speech here.
verses.before: Look, these were the ones who, at Balaam’s counsel, caused the Israelites to act unfaithfully against the LORD in the matter of Peor, so that the plague came upon the congregation of the LORD.
verses.after: “These are the ones who, at Balaam’s advice, led the Israelites to betray the LORD in the affair at Peor, so that a plague struck the LORD’s community.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, these were the ones who, at Balaam’s counsel, caused the Israelites to act unfaithfully against the LORD in the matter of Peor, so that the plague came upon the congregation of the LORD.

verses.rationale: States the commanded killing of children and sexually experienced women explicitly.
verses.before: Now therefore kill every male among the little ones, and kill every woman who has known a man by lying with him.
verses.after: Now kill every boy among the little children, and kill every woman who has slept with a man.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now therefore kill every male among the little ones, and kill every woman who has known a man by lying with him.

verses.rationale: Preserves both survival and the possessive captivity formula without adding an unrecorded fate.
verses.before: But all the young girls who have not known a man by lying with him, keep alive for yourselves.
verses.after: But keep alive for yourselves all the girls who have not slept with a man.
verses.tsw_comparator: But all the young girls who have not known a man by lying with him, keep alive for yourselves.

verses.rationale: Keeps killing and contact as separate grounds and applies both purification days to captives too.
verses.before: Camp outside the camp seven days. Whoever has killed a person and whoever has touched a slain person will purify yourselves on the third day and on the seventh day, you and your captives.
verses.after: Stay outside the camp for seven days. All of you who have killed someone or touched a slain person must purify yourselves on the third and seventh days—you and your captives alike.
verses.tsw_comparator: Camp outside the camp seven days. Whoever has killed a person and whoever has touched a slain person shall purify yourselves on the third day and on the seventh day, you and your captives.

verses.rationale: Retains all four classes of potentially impure possessions.
verses.before: Purify every garment, every article of leather, everything made of goat hair, and every article of wood.”
verses.after: Purify every garment, every leather article, everything made of goats’ hair and every wooden article.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Purify every garment, every article of leather, everything made of goat hair, and every article of wood.”

verses.rationale: Marks the change of speaker to Eleazar and preserves the law formula.
verses.before: Eleazar the priest said to the men of the army who had gone to battle, “This is the statute of the instruction that the LORD commanded Moses:
verses.after: Then Eleazar the priest told the soldiers who had gone to war, “This is the rule of the law that the LORD commanded Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: Eleazar the priest said to the men of the army who had gone to battle, “This is the statute of the instruction that the LORD commanded Moses:

verses.rationale: Keeps all six metals in a sentence continuing into the next verse within one paragraph.
verses.before: Only the gold, silver, bronze, iron, tin, and lead—
verses.after: Gold, silver, bronze, iron, tin and lead—
verses.tsw_comparator: Only the gold, silver, bronze, iron, tin, and lead—

verses.rationale: Preserves the additional water requirement for fire-resistant objects, not an either-or substitution.
verses.before: everything that can withstand fire—you will pass through fire, and it will be clean. Even so, it will also be purified with the water of purification. Whatever cannot withstand fire you will pass through water.
verses.after: anything that can withstand fire must pass through fire and be purified. It must also be purified with the water for removing impurity. Whatever cannot withstand fire must pass through water.
verses.tsw_comparator: everything that can withstand fire—you shall pass through fire, and it shall be clean. Nevertheless, it shall also be purified with the water of purification. Whatever cannot withstand fire you shall pass through water.

verses.rationale: Keeps washing, clean status and reentry in sequence.
verses.before: You will wash your clothes on the seventh day and be clean; afterward you may enter the camp.”
verses.after: Wash your clothes on the seventh day, and you will be clean. After that you may enter the camp.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall wash your clothes on the seventh day and be clean; afterward you may enter the camp.”

verses.rationale: Retains the opening formula for the distribution instruction.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD spoke to Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Names the three parties responsible and preserves people within the count.
verses.before: “Take a count of the plunder that was captured, both people and animals, you and Eleazar the priest and the heads of the ancestral houses of the congregation.
verses.after: “You, Eleazar the priest and the heads of the community’s ancestral houses are to count the captives, both people and animals.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Take a count of the plunder that was captured, both people and animals, you and Eleazar the priest and the heads of the ancestral houses of the congregation.

verses.rationale: Expresses the two equal halves without confusing the whole community with an additional share.
verses.before: Divide the plunder into two parts, between those skilled in war who went out to battle and the whole congregation.
verses.after: Divide the captured people and animals equally between the warriors who went to battle and the rest of the community.
verses.tsw_comparator: Divide the plunder into two parts, between those skilled in war who went out to battle and the whole congregation.

verses.rationale: Retains the one-in-five-hundred levy and its application to people as well as animals.
verses.before: Levy a tribute for the LORD from the warriors who went out to battle: one out of every five hundred, from the people, cattle, donkeys, and flocks.
verses.after: From the soldiers who went to battle, set aside a tribute to the LORD: one out of every five hundred people, cattle, donkeys, sheep and goats.
verses.tsw_comparator: Levy a tribute for the LORD from the warriors who went out to battle: one out of every five hundred, from the people, cattle, donkeys, and flocks.

verses.rationale: Identifies the soldiers’ half as the source and Eleazar as recipient.
verses.before: Take it from their half and give it to Eleazar the priest as the LORD’s contribution.
verses.after: Take it from their half and give it to Eleazar the priest as the LORD’s contribution.
verses.tsw_comparator: Take it from their half and give it to Eleazar the priest as the LORD’s contribution.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes the community’s one-in-fifty levy and its Levitical recipients.
verses.before: From the Israelites’ half you will take one out of every fifty, from the people, cattle, donkeys, flocks, and every kind of livestock, and give them to the Levites who keep charge of the LORD’s tabernacle.”
verses.after: From the Israelites’ half, take one out of every fifty people and animals—cattle, donkeys, sheep, goats and all the livestock. Give them to the Levites who carry out the duties of the LORD’s tabernacle.”
verses.tsw_comparator: From the Israelites’ half you shall take one out of every fifty, from the people, cattle, donkeys, flocks, and every kind of livestock, and give them to the Levites who keep charge of the LORD’s tabernacle.”

verses.rationale: Keeps both executors and the repeated command attribution.
verses.before: Moses and Eleazar the priest did as the LORD commanded Moses.
verses.after: Moses and Eleazar the priest did as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses and Eleazar the priest did as the LORD commanded Moses.

verses.after: The captured property remaining from the soldiers’ plunder included six hundred and seventy-five thousand sheep and goats,
verses.tsw_comparator: The plunder remaining from the spoil that the people of the army had taken was six hundred seventy-five thousand sheep,

verses.before: sixty-one thousand donkeys,
verses.after: sixty-one thousand donkeys,
verses.tsw_comparator: sixty-one thousand donkeys,

verses.rationale: Keeps 32000 human captives and the text’s sexual-experience classification explicit.
verses.before: and thirty-two thousand persons in all, women who had not known a man by lying with him.
verses.after: and thirty-two thousand people, all females who had not slept with a man.
verses.tsw_comparator: and thirty-two thousand persons in all, women who had not known a man by lying with him.

verses.rationale: Preserves 337500 as the soldiers’ exact half of the flocks.
verses.before: The half that was the portion of people who went out to war was three hundred thirty-seven thousand five hundred sheep,
verses.after: The half-share for those who went to war was three hundred and thirty-seven thousand five hundred sheep and goats.
verses.tsw_comparator: The half that was the portion of those who went out to war was three hundred thirty-seven thousand five hundred sheep,

verses.rationale: Preserves the stated 675 tribute, consistent with one in five hundred.
verses.before: and the LORD’s tribute from the sheep was six hundred seventy-five.
verses.after: The LORD’s tribute from the sheep and goats was six hundred and seventy-five.
verses.tsw_comparator: and the LORD’s tribute from the sheep was six hundred seventy-five.

verses.rationale: Keeps both the soldiers’ 36000 cattle and the 72 tribute.
verses.before: The cattle were thirty-six thousand, of which the LORD’s tribute was seventy-two.
verses.after: There were thirty-six thousand cattle, of which the LORD’s tribute was seventy-two.
verses.tsw_comparator: The cattle were thirty-six thousand, of which the LORD’s tribute was seventy-two.

verses.rationale: Preserves 30500 and 61 without rounding.
verses.before: The donkeys were thirty thousand five hundred, of which the LORD’s tribute was sixty-one.
verses.after: There were thirty thousand five hundred donkeys, of which the LORD’s tribute was sixty-one.
verses.tsw_comparator: The donkeys were thirty thousand five hundred, of which the LORD’s tribute was sixty-one.

verses.rationale: Retains the explicit allocation of thirty-two people as tribute.

verses.after: There were sixteen thousand people, of whom the LORD’s tribute was thirty-two people.

verses.after: Moses gave this tribute, the LORD’s contribution, to Eleazar the priest, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses gave the tribute, the LORD’s contribution, to Eleazar the priest, as the LORD commanded Moses.

verses.before: From the Israelites’ half, which Moses had separated from the men who fought—
verses.after: The Israelites’ half, which Moses had separated from the soldiers’ share,
verses.tsw_comparator: From the Israelites’ half, which Moses had separated from the men who fought—

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated 337500 total in the community’s own enumeration.
verses.before: the congregation’s half was three hundred thirty-seven thousand five hundred sheep,
verses.after: was the community’s share: three hundred and thirty-seven thousand five hundred sheep and goats,
verses.tsw_comparator: the congregation’s half was three hundred thirty-seven thousand five hundred sheep,

verses.before: thirty-six thousand cattle,

verses.tsw_comparator: thirty thousand five hundred donkeys,

verses.rationale: Keeps the community’s human captives within the distribution rather than reducing the list to goods.
verses.before: and sixteen thousand persons—
verses.after: and sixteen thousand people.
verses.tsw_comparator: and sixteen thousand persons—

verses.rationale: Preserves the second levy’s fraction, recipients and command formula without adding inferred totals.
verses.before: from the Israelites’ half Moses took one out of every fifty, from both people and animals, and gave them to the Levites who kept charge of the LORD’s tabernacle, as the LORD commanded Moses.
verses.after: From the Israelites’ half, Moses took one out of every fifty people and animals. He gave them to the Levites who carried out the duties of the LORD’s tabernacle, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: from the Israelites’ half Moses took one out of every fifty, from both people and animals, and gave them to the Levites who kept charge of the LORD’s tabernacle, as the LORD commanded Moses.

verses.rationale: Retains both ranks in the renewed approach to Moses.
verses.before: Then the officers who were over the thousands of the army, the commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, came near to Moses.

verses.tsw_comparator: Then the officers who were over the thousands of the army, the commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, came near to Moses.

verses.rationale: Presents the no-loss report as the officers’ own statement.
verses.before: They said to Moses, “Your servants have taken a count of the men of war who were under our command, and not one man of us is missing.
verses.after: They told him, “Your servants have counted the soldiers under our command, and not one of us is missing.
verses.tsw_comparator: They said to Moses, “Your servants have taken a count of the men of war who were under our command, and not one man of us is missing.

verses.rationale: Retains atonement for lives and the five ornament categories, with lexical uncertainty noted in the apparatus.
verses.before: So we have brought the LORD’s offering, what each man found: articles of gold, armlets, bracelets, signet rings, earrings, and necklaces, to make atonement for our lives before the LORD.”
verses.after: So we have brought an offering to the LORD: whatever gold articles each man found—anklets, bracelets, signet rings, earrings and necklaces—to make atonement for our lives before the LORD.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So we have brought the LORD’s offering, what each man found: articles of gold, armlets, bracelets, signet rings, earrings, and necklaces, to make atonement for our lives before the LORD.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the worked-object qualification rather than implying unworked bullion.
verses.before: Moses and Eleazar the priest took the gold from them, all the crafted articles.
verses.after: Moses and Eleazar the priest received their gold, all of it crafted into articles.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses and Eleazar the priest took the gold from them, all the crafted articles.

verses.rationale: Retains both donor ranks and the exact 16750-shekel weight.
verses.before: All the gold of the contribution that they contributed to the LORD, from the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, was sixteen thousand seven hundred fifty shekels.
verses.after: All the gold that the commanders of thousands and of hundreds contributed to the LORD weighed sixteen thousand seven hundred and fifty shekels.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the gold of the contribution that they contributed to the LORD, from the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, was sixteen thousand seven hundred fifty shekels.

verses.rationale: Keeps this parenthetical distinction between individual plunder and the officers’ contribution.
verses.before: The men of war had each taken plunder for themselves.
verses.after: The soldiers had each taken plunder for themselves.
verses.tsw_comparator: The men of war had each taken plunder for themselves.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated recipients, donors and memorial purpose.
verses.before: Moses and Eleazar the priest took the gold from the commanders of thousands and hundreds and brought it into the Tent of Meeting as a remembrance for the Israelites before the LORD.
verses.after: Moses and Eleazar the priest received the gold from the commanders of thousands and of hundreds and brought it into the tent of meeting, as a memorial for the Israelites before the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses and Eleazar the priest took the gold from the commanders of thousands and hundreds and brought it into the Tent of Meeting as a remembrance for the Israelites before the LORD.

verses.rationale: Makes the territorial request’s livestock motive clear while retaining both regions.
verses.before: The descendants of Reuben and the descendants of Gad had very large herds of livestock. They saw the land of Jazer and the land of Gilead, and look—the place was a place for livestock.
verses.after: The Reubenites and Gadites had very large herds. They saw that the lands of Jazer and Gilead were good country for livestock.
verses.tsw_comparator: The descendants of Reuben and the descendants of Gad had very large herds of livestock. They saw the land of Jazer and the land of Gilead, and look—the place was a place for livestock.

verses.rationale: Preserves the reversed tribal order and all three addressed parties in continuing speech introduction.
verses.before: So the descendants of Gad and the descendants of Reuben came and spoke to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the leaders of the congregation, saying,
verses.after: So the Gadites and Reubenites came to Moses, Eleazar the priest and the community’s leaders and said,
verses.tsw_comparator: So the descendants of Gad and the descendants of Reuben came and spoke to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the leaders of the congregation, saying,

verses.rationale: Retains all nine place names as the petitioners’ list continuing into their description.
verses.before: “Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo, and Beon—
verses.after: “Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo and Beon—
verses.tsw_comparator: “Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo, and Beon—

verses.rationale: Keeps the attributed conquest and repeated livestock argument.
verses.before: the land that the LORD struck before the congregation of Israel—is a land for livestock, and your servants have livestock.”
verses.after: the land the LORD struck down before the community of Israel—is livestock country, and your servants have livestock.”
verses.tsw_comparator: the land that the LORD struck before the congregation of Israel—is a land for livestock, and your servants have livestock.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the deferential request and explicit wish not to cross.
verses.before: They said, “If we have found favor in your eyes, let this land be given to your servants as a possession. Do not make us cross the Jordan.”
verses.after: They added, “If we have found favor with you, let this land be given to your servants as our holding. Do not make us cross the Jordan.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They said, “If we have found favor in your eyes, let this land be given to your servants as a possession. Do not make us cross the Jordan.”

verses.rationale: Retains the kinship-based challenge and its accusation of unequal burdens.
verses.before: Moses said to the descendants of Gad and the descendants of Reuben, “Will your brothers go to war while you sit here?

verses.tsw_comparator: Moses said to the descendants of Gad and the descendants of Reuben, “Shall your brothers go to war while you sit here?

verses.rationale: Renders the causative discouragement idiom while binding the full written/read record.

verses.after: Why would you discourage the Israelites from crossing into the land the LORD has given them?
verses.tsw_comparator: Why do you discourage the hearts of the Israelites from crossing into the land that the LORD has given them?

verses.after: That is what your fathers did when I sent them from Kadesh-barnea to look over the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: This is what your fathers did when I sent them from Kadesh-barnea to see the land.

verses.rationale: Retains the sequence of seeing then discouraging and the repeated gift language.
verses.before: They went up to the Wadi Eshcol and saw the land, but they discouraged the hearts of the Israelites so that they did not enter the land the LORD had given them.
verses.after: They went up as far as the Valley of Eshcol and saw the land. Then they discouraged the Israelites from entering the land the LORD had given them.
verses.tsw_comparator: They went up to the Wadi Eshcol and saw the land, but they discouraged the hearts of the Israelites so that they did not enter the land the LORD had given them.

verses.after: The LORD’s anger burned that day, and he swore,
verses.tsw_comparator: The anger of the LORD burned on that day, and the LORD swore, saying,

verses.tsw_comparator: ‘Surely none of the men who came up from Egypt, from twenty years old and upward, shall see the land that I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, because they did not follow me fully,

verses.rationale: Keeps both exceptions, Caleb’s Kenizzite designation and the LORD naming within the oath.
verses.before: except Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite and Joshua son of Nun, because they followed the LORD fully.’
verses.after: except Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite and Joshua son of Nun, for they have followed the LORD wholeheartedly.’
verses.tsw_comparator: except Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite and Joshua son of Nun, because they followed the LORD fully.’

verses.rationale: Preserves forty years and the stated moral characterization of that generation.
verses.before: The anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and the LORD made them wander in the wilderness forty years, until all the generation that had done evil in the eyes of the LORD came to an end.
verses.after: The LORD’s anger burned against Israel, and he made them wander in the wilderness for forty years, until the entire generation that had done evil in his eyes was gone.
verses.tsw_comparator: The anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and the LORD made them wander in the wilderness forty years, until all the generation that had done evil in the eyes of the LORD came to an end.

verses.rationale: Retains the harsh brood accusation and collective consequences rather than neutralizing the rhetoric.
verses.before: And look, you have risen in your fathers’ place, a brood of sinful men, to add still more to the burning anger of the LORD against Israel.
verses.after: And now you have risen up in your fathers’ place, a brood of sinful men, adding still more to the LORD’s burning anger against Israel!
verses.tsw_comparator: And look, you have risen in your fathers’ place, a brood of sinful men, to add still more to the burning anger of the LORD against Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserves Moses’ attribution of prospective destruction to the tribes’ withdrawal.
verses.before: For if you turn away from following the LORD, the LORD will again leave them in the wilderness, and you will destroy all this people.”
verses.after: If you turn away from following him, he will leave them in the wilderness again, and you will destroy this whole people.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For if you turn away from following the LORD, the LORD will again leave them in the wilderness, and you will destroy all this people.”

verses.rationale: Retains the approach and the separate animal and family provisions.
verses.before: Then they came near to him and said, “We will build sheepfolds here for our livestock and cities for our little ones,
verses.after: They came closer to him and said, “Let us build pens here for our livestock and towns for our little children.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they came near to him and said, “We will build sheepfolds here for our livestock and cities for our little ones,

verses.rationale: Preserves military readiness, leading role and the expressed reason for fortified housing.
verses.before: but we ourselves will arm ourselves quickly before the Israelites until we have brought them to their place. Our little ones will live in the fortified cities because of the inhabitants of the land.
verses.after: But we will arm ourselves and move quickly ahead of the Israelites until we have brought them to their place. Meanwhile our little children will live in fortified towns because of the people of the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: but we ourselves will arm ourselves quickly before the Israelites until we have brought them to their place. Our little ones will live in the fortified cities because of the inhabitants of the land.

verses.rationale: Keeps the universal condition for their return, not merely victory in one battle.
verses.before: We will not return to our houses until every Israelite has received an inheritance.
verses.after: We will not return to our homes until every Israelite has received an inheritance.
verses.tsw_comparator: We will not return to our houses until every Israelite has received an inheritance.

verses.rationale: Makes the relative directions explicit while retaining the proposed exclusion from a western share.
verses.before: For we will not inherit with them beyond the Jordan and farther on, because our inheritance has come to us on this eastern side of the Jordan.”
verses.after: We will not take an inheritance with them across the Jordan to the west, because our inheritance has come to us on the east side of the Jordan.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For we will not inherit with them beyond the Jordan and farther on, because our inheritance has come to us on this eastern side of the Jordan.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the conditional beginning and repeated before-the-LORD language.
verses.before: Moses said to them, “If you do this—if you arm yourselves before the LORD for war,
verses.after: Moses answered them, “If you do this—if you arm yourselves before the LORD for war,
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses said to them, “If you do this—if you arm yourselves before the LORD for war,

verses.rationale: Preserves the LORD as the one dispossessing his enemies and the whole armed contingent.
verses.before: and every armed man among you crosses the Jordan before the LORD until the LORD has driven the enemies out from before him,
verses.after: and every armed man among you crosses the Jordan before the LORD until he has driven his enemies out before him,
verses.tsw_comparator: and every armed man among you crosses the Jordan before the LORD until the LORD has driven the enemies out from before him,

verses.rationale: Renders being clear or guiltless as discharge of the stated obligation without erasing its divine and communal dimensions.
verses.before: and the land is subdued before the LORD—then afterward you may return and be free of obligation before the LORD and before Israel, and this land will be your possession before the LORD.
verses.after: and the land has been subdued before the LORD—then you may return, free of your obligation to the LORD and to Israel. This land will be your holding before the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: and the land is subdued before the LORD—then afterward you may return and be free of obligation before the LORD and before Israel, and this land shall be your possession before the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains the familiar personification of sin and its connection with breaking this commitment.
verses.before: But if you do not do so, look—you have sinned against the LORD, and know that your sin will find you.
verses.after: But if you do not do this, you will have sinned against the LORD. Be sure that your sin will find you out.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if you do not do so, look—you have sinned against the LORD, and know that your sin will find you.

verses.rationale: Links the construction permission to fulfillment of the spoken pledge.
verses.before: Build cities for your little ones and folds for your flocks, and do what has gone out from your mouth.”
verses.after: Build towns for your little children and pens for your flocks, and do what you have said you would do.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Build cities for your little ones and folds for your flocks, and do what has gone out from your mouth.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the deferential address without mistaking my lord for the divine name.
verses.before: The descendants of Gad and the descendants of Reuben said to Moses, “Your servants will do as my lord commands.
verses.after: The Gadites and Reubenites said to Moses, “Your servants will do as my lord commands.
verses.tsw_comparator: The descendants of Gad and the descendants of Reuben said to Moses, “Your servants will do as my lord commands.

verses.rationale: Keeps wives, children and the repeated livestock categories separately named.
verses.before: Our little ones, our wives, our livestock, and all our animals will remain there in the cities of Gilead,
verses.after: Our little children, our wives, our herds and all our livestock will stay here in the towns of Gilead.
verses.tsw_comparator: Our little ones, our wives, our livestock, and all our animals will remain there in the cities of Gilead,

verses.rationale: Retains the universal armed commitment and distinguishes LORD from address to Moses.
verses.before: but your servants will cross over, every one armed for war, before the LORD to battle, as my lord says.”
verses.after: But your servants, every man armed for battle, will cross over before the LORD to fight, just as my lord says.”
verses.tsw_comparator: but your servants will cross over, every one armed for war, before the LORD to battle, as my lord says.”

verses.rationale: Names those responsible for implementing the agreement after Moses.
verses.before: So Moses gave command concerning them to Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the ancestral houses of the tribes of the Israelites.
verses.after: Moses gave instructions about them to Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun and the heads of the ancestral houses of Israel’s tribes.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Moses gave command concerning them to Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the ancestral houses of the tribes of the Israelites.

verses.rationale: Preserves the full condition and specific eastern land grant.
verses.before: Moses said to them, “If the descendants of Gad and the descendants of Reuben cross the Jordan with you, everyone armed for battle before the LORD, and the land is subdued before you, then give them the land of Gilead as a possession.
verses.after: He told them, “If the Gadites and Reubenites cross the Jordan with you, every man armed for battle before the LORD, and the land is subdued before you, give them Gilead as their holding.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses said to them, “If the descendants of Gad and the descendants of Reuben cross the Jordan with you, everyone armed for battle before the LORD, and the land is subdued before you, then give them the land of Gilead as a possession.

verses.rationale: Retains the alternative western allotment rather than inventing total disinheritance.
verses.before: But if they do not cross over with you armed, they will receive a possession among you in the land of Canaan.”
verses.after: But if they do not cross over armed with you, they must receive a holding among you in Canaan.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But if they do not cross over with you armed, they shall receive a possession among you in the land of Canaan.”

verses.rationale: Preserves their acknowledgment of the instruction as the LORD’s word.
verses.before: The descendants of Gad and the descendants of Reuben answered, saying, “As the LORD has spoken to your servants, so we will do.
verses.after: The Gadites and Reubenites answered, “What the LORD has told your servants, we will do.
verses.tsw_comparator: The descendants of Gad and the descendants of Reuben answered, saying, “As the LORD has spoken to your servants, so we will do.

verses.rationale: Keeps both their military participation and distinct eastern inheritance.
verses.before: We ourselves will cross over armed before the LORD into the land of Canaan, but the possession of our inheritance will remain with us beyond the Jordan.”
verses.after: We will cross over armed before the LORD into Canaan, while our inherited holding remains on this side of the Jordan.”
verses.tsw_comparator: We ourselves will cross over armed before the LORD into the land of Canaan, but the possession of our inheritance shall remain with us beyond the Jordan.”

verses.rationale: Introduces half-Manasseh where the text does and retains both conquered kingdoms.
verses.before: Moses gave to them—to the descendants of Gad, the descendants of Reuben, and the half-tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph—the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan: the land with its cities and territories, the cities throughout the surrounding land.
verses.after: Moses gave the Gadites, the Reubenites and half the tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph the kingdoms of Sihon king of the Amorites and Og king of Bashan: the land with its towns and their surrounding territory.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses gave to them—to the descendants of Gad, the descendants of Reuben, and the half-tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph—the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan: the land with its cities and territories, the cities throughout the surrounding land.

verses.rationale: Preserves the first three places in a continuous construction list.
verses.before: The descendants of Gad built Dibon, Ataroth, and Aroer,
verses.after: The Gadites rebuilt Dibon, Ataroth and Aroer,
verses.tsw_comparator: The descendants of Gad built Dibon, Ataroth, and Aroer,

verses.rationale: Keeps these three names distinct from the similar Ataroth in the preceding verse.
verses.before: Atroth-shophan, Jazer, and Jogbehah,
verses.after: Atroth-shophan, Jazer and Jogbehah,
verses.tsw_comparator: Atroth-shophan, Jazer, and Jogbehah,

verses.rationale: Completes the Gadite list with both fortified towns and livestock pens.
verses.before: Beth-nimrah and Beth-haran, fortified cities, and folds for sheep.
verses.after: Beth-nimrah and Beth-haran as fortified towns, and they built pens for the flocks.
verses.tsw_comparator: Beth-nimrah and Beth-haran, fortified cities, and folds for sheep.

verses.rationale: Begins the separate Reubenite list without merging tribal territories.
verses.before: The descendants of Reuben built Heshbon, Elealeh, and Kiriathaim,
verses.after: The Reubenites rebuilt Heshbon, Elealeh and Kiriathaim,
verses.tsw_comparator: The descendants of Reuben built Heshbon, Elealeh, and Kiriathaim,

verses.rationale: Preserves the renaming notice without supplying unknown replacement names.
verses.before: Nebo and Baal-meon—their names being changed—and Sibmah. They gave names to the cities they built.
verses.after: Nebo and Baal-meon, whose names were changed, and Sibmah. They gave names to the towns they rebuilt.
verses.tsw_comparator: Nebo and Baal-meon—their names being changed—and Sibmah. They gave names to the cities they built.

verses.rationale: Renders Machir’s family as the collective actor across the Hebrew shift to singular dispossession.
verses.before: The descendants of Machir son of Manasseh went to Gilead, captured it, and dispossessed the Amorites who were in it.
verses.after: The descendants of Machir son of Manasseh went to Gilead and captured it, driving out the Amorites who lived there.
verses.tsw_comparator: The descendants of Machir son of Manasseh went to Gilead, captured it, and dispossessed the Amorites who were in it.

verses.rationale: Keeps the named ancestor while making the collective settlement reference understandable.
verses.before: Moses gave Gilead to Machir son of Manasseh, and he lived in it.
verses.after: Moses gave Gilead to Machir son of Manasseh, and Machir’s family settled there.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses gave Gilead to Machir son of Manasseh, and he lived in it.

verses.rationale: Uses descendant for the genealogical son designation without inventing an immediate father relationship.
verses.before: Jair son of Manasseh went and captured their villages and called them Havvoth-jair.
verses.after: Jair, a descendant of Manasseh, went and captured their villages, and called them Havvoth-jair.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jair son of Manasseh went and captured their villages and called them Havvoth-jair.

verses.rationale: Preserves the separate conquest and explicit self-naming.
verses.before: Nobah went and captured Kenath and its villages and called it Nobah after his own name.
verses.after: Nobah went and captured Kenath and its surrounding villages. He named it Nobah after himself.
verses.tsw_comparator: Nobah went and captured Kenath and its villages and called it Nobah after his own name.

verses.rationale: Keeps the itinerary as an organized departure under two named leaders.
verses.before: These are the stages of the Israelites when they went out from the land of Egypt by their divisions under the hand of Moses and Aaron.
verses.after: These are the stages of the Israelites’ journey when they came out of Egypt in their divisions under the leadership of Moses and Aaron.
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the stages of the Israelites when they went out from the land of Egypt by their divisions under the hand of Moses and Aaron.

verses.rationale: Preserves the reciprocal departure-stage wording and notes the command phrase’s possible attachment.
verses.before: Moses wrote down their starting points according to their stages at the command of the LORD. These are their stages according to their starting points.
verses.after: At the LORD’s command, Moses recorded their departures, stage by stage. These are the stages of their journey, listed by departure point.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses wrote down their starting points according to their stages at the command of the LORD. These are their stages according to their starting points.

verses.rationale: Retains the exact date and ancient raised-hand image, explained selectively in vocabulary.
verses.before: They set out from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month. On the day after the Passover the Israelites went out with a high hand in the sight of all the Egyptians,
verses.after: They left Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of that month. On the day after Passover, the Israelites went out with a raised hand, in full view of all the Egyptians.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month. On the day after the Passover the Israelites went out with a high hand in the sight of all the Egyptians,

verses.rationale: Preserves the simultaneous burial and the distinct judgment against Egypt’s gods.
verses.before: while the Egyptians were burying all their firstborn whom the LORD had struck among them. The LORD also executed judgments against their gods.
verses.after: The Egyptians were burying all their firstborn whom the LORD had struck down among them. The LORD had also carried out judgments against their gods.
verses.tsw_comparator: while the Egyptians were burying all their firstborn whom the LORD had struck among them. The LORD also executed judgments against their gods.

verses.rationale: Keeps the itinerary’s first repeated departure-and-camp pair. Uses “left” for the repeated departure verb while keeping the source’s itinerary formula.
verses.before: The Israelites set out from Rameses and camped at Succoth.
verses.after: The Israelites left Rameses and camped at Succoth.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Israelites set out from Rameses and camped at Succoth.

verses.rationale: Preserves Etham and its wilderness-edge location.
verses.before: They set out from Succoth and camped at Etham, which is at the edge of the wilderness.
verses.after: They left Succoth and camped at Etham, on the edge of the wilderness.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from Succoth and camped at Etham, which is at the edge of the wilderness.

verses.rationale: Retains the turn and all three geographical markers without inventing a route map.
verses.before: They set out from Etham and turned back to Pi-hahiroth, which faces Baal-zephon, and they camped before Migdol.
verses.after: They left Etham and turned back toward Pi-hahiroth, opposite Baal-zephon, and camped near Migdol.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from Etham and turned back to Pi-hahiroth, which faces Baal-zephon, and they camped before Migdol.

verses.rationale: Keeps the Hahiroth form, sea crossing, three days and Etham designation without harmonizing to another itinerary.
verses.before: They set out from before Hahiroth, crossed through the midst of the sea into the wilderness, went a journey of three days in the wilderness of Etham, and camped at Marah.
verses.after: They left their camp opposite Hahiroth and passed through the middle of the sea into the wilderness. They traveled for three days in the wilderness of Etham and camped at Marah.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from before Hahiroth, crossed through the midst of the sea into the wilderness, went a journey of three days in the wilderness of Etham, and camped at Marah.

verses.rationale: Preserves both exact counts and the repeated Elim name.
verses.before: They set out from Marah and came to Elim. At Elim were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they camped there.
verses.after: They left Marah and came to Elim. At Elim there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they camped there.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from Marah and came to Elim. At Elim were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they camped there.

verses.rationale: Retains the sea’s Hebrew name consistently with earlier Fluent passages.
verses.before: They set out from Elim and camped by the Red Sea.
verses.after: They left Elim and camped by the Sea of Reeds.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from Elim and camped by the Red Sea.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes Sin from the later wilderness of Zin.
verses.before: They set out from the Red Sea and camped in the wilderness of Sin.
verses.after: They left the Sea of Reeds and camped in the wilderness of Sin.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from the Red Sea and camped in the wilderness of Sin.

verses.rationale: Preserves the Sin-to-Dophkah stage and formula. Uses “left” for the repeated departure verb while keeping the source’s itinerary formula.
verses.before: They set out from the wilderness of Sin and camped at Dophkah.
verses.after: They left the wilderness of Sin and camped at Dophkah.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from the wilderness of Sin and camped at Dophkah.

verses.rationale: Preserves the Dophkah-to-Alush stage without compressing the list. Uses “left” for the repeated departure verb while keeping the source’s itinerary formula.
verses.before: They set out from Dophkah and camped at Alush.
verses.after: They left Dophkah and camped at Alush.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from Dophkah and camped at Alush.

verses.rationale: Keeps the water shortage attached specifically to Rephidim. Uses “left” for the repeated departure verb while keeping the source’s itinerary formula.
verses.before: They set out from Alush and camped at Rephidim, where there was no water for the people to drink.
verses.after: They left Alush and camped at Rephidim, where there was no water for the people to drink.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from Alush and camped at Rephidim, where there was no water for the people to drink.

verses.rationale: Preserves Sinai’s wilderness designation. Uses “left” for the repeated departure verb while keeping the source’s itinerary formula.
verses.before: They set out from Rephidim and camped in the wilderness of Sinai.
verses.after: They left Rephidim and camped in the wilderness of Sinai.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from Rephidim and camped in the wilderness of Sinai.

verses.rationale: Retains the complete place name and the recurring travel formula. Uses “left” for the repeated departure verb while keeping the source’s itinerary formula.
verses.before: They set out from the wilderness of Sinai and camped at Kibroth-hattaavah.
verses.after: They left the wilderness of Sinai and camped at Kibroth-hattaavah.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from the wilderness of Sinai and camped at Kibroth-hattaavah.

verses.rationale: Preserves the Kibroth-hattaavah-to-Hazeroth stage. Uses “left” for the repeated departure verb while keeping the source’s itinerary formula.
verses.before: They set out from Kibroth-hattaavah and camped at Hazeroth.
verses.after: They left Kibroth-hattaavah and camped at Hazeroth.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from Kibroth-hattaavah and camped at Hazeroth.

verses.rationale: Keeps Rithmah as its own itinerary stop. Uses “left” for the repeated departure verb while keeping the source’s itinerary formula.
verses.before: They set out from Hazeroth and camped at Rithmah.
verses.after: They left Hazeroth and camped at Rithmah.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from Hazeroth and camped at Rithmah.

verses.rationale: Preserves the compound name Rimmon-perez. Uses “left” for the repeated departure verb while keeping the source’s itinerary formula.
verses.before: They set out from Rithmah and camped at Rimmon-perez.
verses.after: They left Rithmah and camped at Rimmon-perez.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from Rithmah and camped at Rimmon-perez.

verses.rationale: Retains the exact adjacent departure and arrival locations. Uses “left” for the repeated departure verb while keeping the source’s itinerary formula.
verses.before: They set out from Rimmon-perez and camped at Libnah.
verses.after: They left Rimmon-perez and camped at Libnah.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from Rimmon-perez and camped at Libnah.

verses.rationale: Keeps the Libnah-to-Rissah stage and deliberate repetition. Uses “left” for the repeated departure verb while keeping the source’s itinerary formula.
verses.before: They set out from Libnah and camped at Rissah.
verses.after: They left Libnah and camped at Rissah.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from Libnah and camped at Rissah.

verses.rationale: Preserves Kehelathah without merging similar later names. Uses “left” for the repeated departure verb while keeping the source’s itinerary formula.
verses.before: They set out from Rissah and camped at Kehelathah.
verses.after: They left Rissah and camped at Kehelathah.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from Rissah and camped at Kehelathah.

verses.rationale: Retains the mountain designation at Shepher. Uses “left” for the repeated departure verb while keeping the source’s itinerary formula.
verses.before: They set out from Kehelathah and camped at Mount Shepher.
verses.after: They left Kehelathah and camped at Mount Shepher.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from Kehelathah and camped at Mount Shepher.

verses.rationale: Keeps Mount Shepher as the departure point and Haradah as the next camp. Uses “left” for the repeated departure verb while keeping the source’s itinerary formula.
verses.before: They set out from Mount Shepher and camped at Haradah.
verses.after: They left Mount Shepher and camped at Haradah.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from Mount Shepher and camped at Haradah.

verses.rationale: Preserves Makheloth as distinct from Kehelathah. Uses “left” for the repeated departure verb while keeping the source’s itinerary formula.
verses.before: They set out from Haradah and camped at Makheloth.
verses.after: They left Haradah and camped at Makheloth.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from Haradah and camped at Makheloth.

verses.rationale: Retains the Makheloth-to-Tahath stage. Uses “left” for the repeated departure verb while keeping the source’s itinerary formula.
verses.before: They set out from Makheloth and camped at Tahath.
verses.after: They left Makheloth and camped at Tahath.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from Makheloth and camped at Tahath.

verses.rationale: Keeps the short but distinct Tahath and Terah names. Uses “left” for the repeated departure verb while keeping the source’s itinerary formula.
verses.before: They set out from Tahath and camped at Terah.
verses.after: They left Tahath and camped at Terah.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from Tahath and camped at Terah.

verses.rationale: Preserves Mithkah as a separate station. Uses “left” for the repeated departure verb while keeping the source’s itinerary formula.
verses.before: They set out from Terah and camped at Mithkah.
verses.after: They left Terah and camped at Mithkah.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from Terah and camped at Mithkah.

verses.rationale: Retains the recorded sequence into Hashmonah. Uses “left” for the repeated departure verb while keeping the source’s itinerary formula.
verses.before: They set out from Mithkah and camped at Hashmonah.
verses.after: They left Mithkah and camped at Hashmonah.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from Mithkah and camped at Hashmonah.

verses.rationale: Preserves the plural-form place name Moseroth without harmonizing another account. Uses “left” for the repeated departure verb while keeping the source’s itinerary formula.
verses.before: They set out from Hashmonah and camped at Moseroth.
verses.after: They left Hashmonah and camped at Moseroth.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from Hashmonah and camped at Moseroth.

verses.rationale: Keeps the full Bene-jaakan place name. Uses “left” for the repeated departure verb while keeping the source’s itinerary formula.
verses.before: They set out from Moseroth and camped at Bene-jaakan.
verses.after: They left Moseroth and camped at Bene-jaakan.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from Moseroth and camped at Bene-jaakan.

verses.rationale: Retains Hor-haggidgad as distinct from Mount Hor. Uses “left” for the repeated departure verb while keeping the source’s itinerary formula.
verses.before: They set out from Bene-jaakan and camped at Hor-haggidgad.
verses.after: They left Bene-jaakan and camped at Hor-haggidgad.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from Bene-jaakan and camped at Hor-haggidgad.

verses.rationale: Preserves the next named stage and formula. Uses “left” for the repeated departure verb while keeping the source’s itinerary formula.
verses.before: They set out from Hor-haggidgad and camped at Jotbathah.
verses.after: They left Hor-haggidgad and camped at Jotbathah.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from Hor-haggidgad and camped at Jotbathah.

verses.rationale: Keeps Abronah in the itinerary without omission. Uses “left” for the repeated departure verb while keeping the source’s itinerary formula.
verses.before: They set out from Jotbathah and camped at Abronah.
verses.after: They left Jotbathah and camped at Abronah.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from Jotbathah and camped at Abronah.

verses.rationale: Retains the complete Ezion-geber name. Uses “left” for the repeated departure verb while keeping the source’s itinerary formula.
verses.before: They set out from Abronah and camped at Ezion-geber.
verses.after: They left Abronah and camped at Ezion-geber.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from Abronah and camped at Ezion-geber.

verses.rationale: Preserves the explicit Kadesh identification and Zin rather than Sin.
verses.before: They set out from Ezion-geber and camped at Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin.
verses.after: They left Ezion-geber and camped in the wilderness of Zin, that is, Kadesh.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from Ezion-geber and camped at Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin.

verses.rationale: Locates this Mount Hor by Edom, important for distinguishing the northern boundary mountain.
verses.before: They set out from Kadesh and camped at Mount Hor, at the edge of the land of Edom.
verses.after: They left Kadesh and camped at Mount Hor, on the edge of the land of Edom.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from Kadesh and camped at Mount Hor, at the edge of the land of Edom.

verses.rationale: Preserves Aaron’s office, divine command and all components of the death date.
verses.before: Aaron the priest went up Mount Hor at the command of the LORD and died there, in the fortieth year after the Israelites came out from the land of Egypt, in the fifth month, on the first day of the month.
verses.after: At the LORD’s command, Aaron the priest went up Mount Hor and died there. It was the first day of the fifth month in the fortieth year after the Israelites came out of Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: Aaron the priest went up Mount Hor at the command of the LORD and died there, in the fortieth year after the Israelites came out from the land of Egypt, in the fifth month, on the first day of the month.

verses.rationale: Keeps the exact age 123 and repeated death location.
verses.before: Aaron was one hundred twenty-three years old when he died on Mount Hor.
verses.after: Aaron was one hundred and twenty-three years old when he died on Mount Hor.
verses.tsw_comparator: Aaron was one hundred twenty-three years old when he died on Mount Hor.

verses.rationale: Retains this notice without adding the battle described elsewhere.
verses.before: The Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev in the land of Canaan, heard of the coming of the Israelites.
verses.after: The Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev in the land of Canaan, heard that the Israelites were coming.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev in the land of Canaan, heard of the coming of the Israelites.

verses.rationale: Resumes the itinerary after the death and Arad notices. Uses “left” for the repeated departure verb while keeping the source’s itinerary formula.
verses.before: They set out from Mount Hor and camped at Zalmonah.
verses.after: They left Mount Hor and camped at Zalmonah.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from Mount Hor and camped at Zalmonah.

verses.rationale: Preserves the Zalmonah-to-Punon stage. Uses “left” for the repeated departure verb while keeping the source’s itinerary formula.
verses.before: They set out from Zalmonah and camped at Punon.
verses.after: They left Zalmonah and camped at Punon.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from Zalmonah and camped at Punon.

verses.rationale: Keeps Oboth as the next distinct camp. Uses “left” for the repeated departure verb while keeping the source’s itinerary formula.
verses.before: They set out from Punon and camped at Oboth.
verses.after: They left Punon and camped at Oboth.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from Punon and camped at Oboth.

verses.rationale: Preserves the full Iye-abarim name and Moab-border location. Uses “left” for the repeated departure verb while keeping the source’s itinerary formula.
verses.before: They set out from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim, on the border of Moab.
verses.after: They left Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim, on the border of Moab.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim, on the border of Moab.

verses.rationale: Retains the shortened Iyim form instead of silently replacing it with the preceding full name. Uses “left” for the repeated departure verb while keeping the source’s itinerary formula.
verses.before: They set out from Iyim and camped at Dibon-gad.
verses.after: They left Iyim and camped at Dibon-gad.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from Iyim and camped at Dibon-gad.

verses.rationale: Keeps both compound place names and their order. Uses “left” for the repeated departure verb while keeping the source’s itinerary formula.
verses.before: They set out from Dibon-gad and camped at Almon-diblathaim.
verses.after: They left Dibon-gad and camped at Almon-diblathaim.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from Dibon-gad and camped at Almon-diblathaim.

verses.rationale: Preserves the mountain range and its relation to Nebo.
verses.before: They set out from Almon-diblathaim and camped in the mountains of Abarim before Nebo.
verses.after: They left Almon-diblathaim and camped in the mountains of Abarim, opposite Nebo.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from Almon-diblathaim and camped in the mountains of Abarim before Nebo.

verses.rationale: Retains the final camp’s three geographical references.
verses.before: They set out from the mountains of Abarim and camped in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho.
verses.after: They left the mountains of Abarim and camped on the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from the mountains of Abarim and camped in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho.

verses.rationale: Makes the camp’s extent clear while preserving both endpoints.
verses.before: They camped by the Jordan from Beth-jeshimoth as far as Abel-shittim in the plains of Moab.
verses.after: Their camp stretched along the Jordan from Beth-jeshimoth to Abel-shittim, on the plains of Moab.
verses.tsw_comparator: They camped by the Jordan from Beth-jeshimoth as far as Abel-shittim in the plains of Moab.

verses.rationale: Keeps the full repeated setting as the itinerary shifts to instruction.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho, saying,
verses.after: There on the plains of Moab, by the Jordan across from Jericho, the LORD spoke to Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves the instruction’s entry condition in a sentence continuing into the next verse.
verses.before: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
verses.after: “Tell the Israelites: When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
verses.tsw_comparator: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan,

verses.rationale: Keeps dispossession explicit and distinguishes three cultic objects or sites, with uncertainty over figured stones noted.
verses.before: you will drive out all the inhabitants of the land from before you, destroy all their carved stones, destroy all their cast images, and demolish all their high places.
verses.after: you must drive out all the land’s inhabitants before you. Destroy all their figured stones and all their cast images, and demolish all their high places.
verses.tsw_comparator: you shall drive out all the inhabitants of the land from before you, destroy all their carved stones, destroy all their cast images, and demolish all their high places.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated possession language and stated gift rationale.
verses.before: You will take possession of the land and live in it, for I have given the land to you to possess it.
verses.after: Take possession of the land and settle in it, for I have given you the land to possess.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall take possession of the land and live in it, for I have given the land to you to possess it.

verses.rationale: Preserves both proportional allocation and lot, without inventing their precise administrative combination.
verses.before: You will distribute the land by lot according to your clans. To a larger group you will give a larger inheritance, and to a smaller group you will give a smaller inheritance. Wherever the lot falls for each, there will the inheritance be. According to your ancestral tribes you will inherit.
verses.after: Divide the land by lot among your clans. Give a larger inheritance to a larger group and a smaller inheritance to a smaller group. Each group will have the place its lot falls on; take your inheritance according to your ancestral tribes.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall distribute the land by lot according to your clans. To a larger group you shall give a larger inheritance, and to a smaller group you shall give a smaller inheritance. Wherever the lot falls for each, there shall the inheritance be. According to your ancestral tribes you shall inherit.

verses.rationale: Retains the painful bodily imagery and the warning’s stated condition.
verses.before: But if you do not drive out the inhabitants of the land from before you, then those whom you allow to remain will become barbs in your eyes and thorns in your sides, and they will harass you in the land where you live.
verses.after: But if you do not drive out the land’s inhabitants before you, those you leave will be barbs in your eyes and thorns in your sides. They will harass you in the land where you settle.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if you do not drive out the inhabitants of the land from before you, then those whom you allow to remain shall become barbs in your eyes and thorns in your sides, and they shall harass you in the land where you live.

verses.rationale: Keeps the reversal directed against Israel without qualifying away its force.
verses.before: And then, as I intended to do to them, so I will do to you.”
verses.after: And what I planned to do to them, I will do to you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And then, as I intended to do to them, so I will do to you.”

verses.rationale: Retains the opening divine speech formula for the boundaries.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD spoke to Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Keeps inheritance by allotted territory and the Canaan designation.
verses.before: “Command the Israelites and say to them: When you enter the land of Canaan, this is the land that will fall to you as an inheritance, the land of Canaan according to its boundaries.
verses.after: “Command the Israelites: When you enter the land of Canaan, this is the land that will fall to you as an inheritance—Canaan within these borders.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Command the Israelites and say to them: When you enter the land of Canaan, this is the land that shall fall to you as an inheritance, the land of Canaan according to its boundaries.

verses.rationale: Preserves Zin, Edom and the eastern end of the sea without adding a modern map.
verses.before: Your southern side will extend from the wilderness of Zin along the side of Edom. Your southern boundary will begin at the end of the Salt Sea on the east.
verses.after: Your southern side will run from the wilderness of Zin along Edom. Your southern boundary will begin at the eastern end of the Salt Sea.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your southern side shall extend from the wilderness of Zin along the side of Edom. Your southern boundary shall begin at the end of the Salt Sea on the east.

verses.rationale: Keeps all boundary turns and names, with the full written/read annotation bound.
verses.before: Your boundary will turn south of the Ascent of Akrabbim and pass along to Zin. Its extent will be south of Kadesh-barnea. Then it will go out to Hazar-addar and pass along to Azmon.
verses.after: Your boundary will turn south of the Ascent of Akrabbim and pass through Zin, reaching south of Kadesh-barnea. It will go on to Hazar-addar and pass through Azmon.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your boundary shall turn south of the Ascent of Akrabbim and pass along to Zin. Its extent shall be south of Kadesh-barnea. Then it shall go out to Hazar-addar and pass along to Azmon.

verses.rationale: Retains a wadi rather than identifying it as the Nile or asserting an uncertain modern location.
verses.before: The boundary will turn from Azmon to the Wadi of Egypt, and its end will be at the sea.
verses.after: From Azmon the boundary will turn toward the Wadi of Egypt and end at the sea.
verses.tsw_comparator: The boundary shall turn from Azmon to the Wadi of Egypt, and its end shall be at the sea.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated western-boundary formula and coast expression.
verses.before: For the western boundary, the Great Sea and its coastline will be your boundary. This will be your western boundary.
verses.after: Your western boundary will be the Great Sea and its coast. This will be your western boundary.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the western boundary, the Great Sea and its coastline shall be your boundary. This shall be your western boundary.

verses.rationale: Retains the northern Mount Hor without conflating it with Aaron’s death site.
verses.before: This will be your northern boundary: from the Great Sea you will mark out a line to Mount Hor.
verses.after: This will be your northern boundary: mark a line from the Great Sea to Mount Hor.
verses.tsw_comparator: This shall be your northern boundary: from the Great Sea you shall mark out a line to Mount Hor.

verses.rationale: Treats Lebo-hamath as a place designation while noting the entrance-to-Hamath alternative.
verses.before: From Mount Hor you will mark it to Lebo-hamath, and the boundary will extend to Zedad.
verses.after: From Mount Hor mark a line to Lebo-hamath, with the boundary reaching Zedad.
verses.tsw_comparator: From Mount Hor you shall mark it to Lebo-hamath, and the boundary shall extend to Zedad.

verses.rationale: Preserves both final northern points and the closing formula.
verses.before: Then the boundary will extend to Ziphron, and its end will be at Hazar-enan. This will be your northern boundary.
verses.after: Then the boundary will run to Ziphron and end at Hazar-enan. This will be your northern boundary.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the boundary shall extend to Ziphron, and its end shall be at Hazar-enan. This shall be your northern boundary.

verses.rationale: Keeps Shepham as the first named eastern segment.
verses.before: You will mark out your eastern boundary from Hazar-enan to Shepham.
verses.after: Mark your eastern boundary from Hazar-enan to Shepham.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall mark out your eastern boundary from Hazar-enan to Shepham.

verses.rationale: Preserves the descending route, Ain relation and eastern shoulder or ridge of the lake.
verses.before: The boundary will go down from Shepham to Riblah on the east side of Ain. The boundary will go down and reach the eastern slope of the Sea of Chinnereth.
verses.after: The boundary will go down from Shepham to Riblah, east of Ain. It will continue down and touch the ridge east of the Sea of Chinnereth.
verses.tsw_comparator: The boundary shall go down from Shepham to Riblah on the east side of Ain. The boundary shall go down and reach the eastern slope of the Sea of Chinnereth.

verses.rationale: Closes the boundary circuit with Jordan and Salt Sea without changing the earlier southern starting point.
verses.before: Then the boundary will go down to the Jordan, and its end will be at the Salt Sea. This will be your land according to its boundaries all around.”
verses.after: Then the boundary will go down along the Jordan and end at the Salt Sea. This will be your land, with its boundaries on every side.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the boundary shall go down to the Jordan, and its end shall be at the Salt Sea. This shall be your land according to its boundaries all around.”

verses.rationale: Retains allocation by lot and the exact nine-and-a-half tribal grouping.
verses.before: Moses commanded the Israelites, saying, “This is the land that you will receive by lot as an inheritance, which the LORD has commanded to give to the nine tribes and the half-tribe.
verses.after: Moses commanded the Israelites, “This is the land you are to receive as an inheritance by lot. The LORD has commanded that it be given to the nine tribes and the half-tribe.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses commanded the Israelites, saying, “This is the land that you shall receive by lot as an inheritance, which the LORD has commanded to give to the nine tribes and the half-tribe.

verses.rationale: Keeps each eastern tribal group and the repeated ancestral-house qualification.
verses.before: For the tribe of the Reubenites by their ancestral houses and the tribe of the Gadites by their ancestral houses have received their inheritance, and the half-tribe of Manasseh has received its inheritance.
verses.after: The tribe of Reuben, by its ancestral houses, and the tribe of Gad, by its ancestral houses, have already received their inheritance, as has half the tribe of Manasseh.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the tribe of the Reubenites by their ancestral houses and the tribe of the Gadites by their ancestral houses have received their inheritance, and the half-tribe of Manasseh has received its inheritance.

verses.rationale: Retains both numerical grouping and the east/sunrise repetition.
verses.before: The two tribes and the half-tribe have received their inheritance beyond the Jordan at Jericho, eastward, toward the sunrise.”
verses.after: Those two tribes and the half-tribe have received their inheritance across the Jordan from Jericho, on the east, toward the sunrise.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The two tribes and the half-tribe have received their inheritance beyond the Jordan at Jericho, eastward, toward the sunrise.”

verses.rationale: Marks a new divine instruction introducing the allotment leaders.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD spoke to Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Identifies the two principal allocators and Eleazar’s priestly role.
verses.before: “These are the names of the men who will divide the land for you as inheritance: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun.
verses.after: “These are the men who will assign the land to you as an inheritance: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun.
verses.tsw_comparator: “These are the names of the men who shall divide the land for you as inheritance: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun.

verses.rationale: Preserves one leader per tribe and their specific allotment task.
verses.before: You will take one leader from each tribe to divide the land as inheritance.
verses.after: Take one leader from each tribe to assign the land as an inheritance.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall take one leader from each tribe to divide the land as inheritance.

verses.rationale: Begins the list with Caleb’s full identification, continuing through the subsequent verses.
verses.before: These are the names of the men: from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
verses.after: These are their names: from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the names of the men: from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;

verses.rationale: Preserves Shemuel, his father and tribe without substituting the later familiar Samuel spelling.
verses.before: from the tribe of the Simeonites, Shemuel son of Ammihud;
verses.after: from the tribe of Simeon, Shemuel son of Ammihud;
verses.tsw_comparator: from the tribe of the Simeonites, Shemuel son of Ammihud;

verses.rationale: Keeps the complete Benjamin allocation-leader pair.
verses.before: from the tribe of Benjamin, Elidad son of Chislon;
verses.after: from the tribe of Benjamin, Elidad son of Chislon;
verses.tsw_comparator: from the tribe of Benjamin, Elidad son of Chislon;

verses.rationale: Retains the explicit leader title where it appears in this list.
verses.before: from the tribe of the Danites, the leader Bukki son of Jogli;
verses.after: from the tribe of Dan, the leader Bukki son of Jogli;
verses.tsw_comparator: from the tribe of the Danites, the leader Bukki son of Jogli;

verses.rationale: Keeps the additional Joseph ancestry and Manasseh’s named representative.
verses.before: from the descendants of Joseph, from the tribe of the Manassites, the leader Hanniel son of Ephod;
verses.after: from the descendants of Joseph, from the tribe of Manasseh, the leader Hanniel son of Ephod;
verses.tsw_comparator: from the descendants of Joseph, from the tribe of the Manassites, the leader Hanniel son of Ephod;

verses.rationale: Preserves Ephraim’s distinct leader and patronymic.
verses.before: from the tribe of the Ephraimites, the leader Kemuel son of Shiphtan;
