verses.after: from the tribe of Ephraim, the leader Kemuel son of Shiphtan;
verses.tsw_comparator: from the tribe of the Ephraimites, the leader Kemuel son of Shiphtan;

verses.rationale: Retains Zebulun and the complete Elizaphan-Parnach pairing.
verses.before: from the tribe of the Zebulunites, the leader Elizaphan son of Parnach;
verses.after: from the tribe of Zebulun, the leader Elizaphan son of Parnach;
verses.tsw_comparator: from the tribe of the Zebulunites, the leader Elizaphan son of Parnach;

verses.rationale: Preserves the tribe and both names in the continuing list.
verses.before: from the tribe of the Issacharites, the leader Paltiel son of Azzan;
verses.after: from the tribe of Issachar, the leader Paltiel son of Azzan;
verses.tsw_comparator: from the tribe of the Issacharites, the leader Paltiel son of Azzan;

verses.rationale: Distinguishes Ahihud from the similar Ammihud in other entries.
verses.before: from the tribe of the Asherites, the leader Ahihud son of Shelomi;
verses.after: from the tribe of Asher, the leader Ahihud son of Shelomi;
verses.tsw_comparator: from the tribe of the Asherites, the leader Ahihud son of Shelomi;

verses.rationale: Completes the ten-member list with Naphtali’s full identification.
verses.before: from the tribe of the Naphtalites, the leader Pedahel son of Ammihud.”
verses.after: and from the tribe of Naphtali, the leader Pedahel son of Ammihud.”
verses.tsw_comparator: from the tribe of the Naphtalites, the leader Pedahel son of Ammihud.”

verses.rationale: Retains the closing divine appointment and geographic scope.
verses.before: These are the ones whom the LORD commanded to allot the inheritance to the Israelites in the land of Canaan.
verses.after: These are the men the LORD commanded to assign the Israelites their inheritance in the land of Canaan.
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the ones whom the LORD commanded to allot the inheritance to the Israelites in the land of Canaan.

verses.rationale: Preserves the location formula linking the town and refuge rules to the final camp.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho, saying,
verses.after: On the plains of Moab, by the Jordan across from Jericho, the LORD spoke to Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho, saying,

verses.rationale: Keeps the towns as contributions from tribal holdings and the surrounding pasture requirement.
verses.before: “Command the Israelites to give to the Levites from the inheritance of their possession cities to live in, and give the Levites pasturelands around the cities.
verses.after: “Command the Israelites to give the Levites towns to live in out of the land they hold as an inheritance. They must also give the Levites pastureland around those towns.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Command the Israelites to give to the Levites from the inheritance of their possession cities to live in, and give the Levites pasturelands around the cities.

verses.rationale: Retains the overlapping livelihood categories rather than deleting apparent redundancy; the final term is noted.
verses.before: The cities will be for them to live in, and their pasturelands will be for their livestock, their possessions, and all their animals.
verses.after: The towns will be theirs to live in, and the pastureland will be for their animals, their possessions and all their livestock.
verses.tsw_comparator: The cities shall be for them to live in, and their pasturelands shall be for their livestock, their possessions, and all their animals.

verses.rationale: Preserves the explicit 1000-cubit outward measure without reconciling it away against the next verse.
verses.before: The pasturelands of the cities that you give the Levites will extend from the city wall outward one thousand cubits all around.
verses.after: The pastureland you give the Levites must extend a thousand cubits outward from the town wall, all around.
verses.tsw_comparator: The pasturelands of the cities that you give the Levites shall extend from the city wall outward one thousand cubits all around.

verses.rationale: Retains all four 2000-cubit measures and central town without inventing a geometric resolution.
verses.before: Outside the city you will measure two thousand cubits on the east side, two thousand on the south side, two thousand on the west side, and two thousand on the north side, with the city in the middle. This will be for them as pasturelands for the cities.
verses.after: Outside the town, measure two thousand cubits on the east side, two thousand on the south, two thousand on the west and two thousand on the north, with the town in the middle. This will be their towns’ pastureland.
verses.tsw_comparator: Outside the city you shall measure two thousand cubits on the east side, two thousand on the south side, two thousand on the west side, and two thousand on the north side, with the city in the middle. This shall be for them as pasturelands for the cities.

verses.rationale: Keeps six refuge towns plus forty-two others and avoids prejudging every killer as a murderer.
verses.before: The cities that you give the Levites will include six cities of refuge, which you will provide so that a manslayer may flee there; in addition to these you will give forty-two cities.
verses.after: Among the towns you give the Levites, six are to be refuge towns, where a person who has killed someone can flee. In addition, give them forty-two towns.
verses.tsw_comparator: The cities that you give the Levites shall include six cities of refuge, which you shall provide so that a manslayer may flee there; in addition to these you shall give forty-two cities.

verses.rationale: Preserves the stated total 48 and associated land.
verses.before: All the cities that you give the Levites will be forty-eight cities, together with their pasturelands.
verses.after: Altogether you must give the Levites forty-eight towns, with their pastureland.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the cities that you give the Levites shall be forty-eight cities, together with their pasturelands.

verses.rationale: Keeps both repeated proportional rules and the inheritance basis.
verses.before: As for the cities you give from the possession of the Israelites, from the larger tribe you will take more, and from the smaller tribe you will take fewer. Each tribe will give some of its cities to the Levites in proportion to the inheritance it receives.”
verses.after: The towns you give from the Israelites’ holdings must be proportionate: take more from a larger group and fewer from a smaller one. Each must give towns to the Levites in proportion to the inheritance it receives.”
verses.tsw_comparator: As for the cities you give from the possession of the Israelites, from the larger tribe you shall take more, and from the smaller tribe you shall take fewer. Each tribe shall give some of its cities to the Levites in proportion to the inheritance it receives.”

verses.rationale: Marks the new speech specifying refuge procedures.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD spoke to Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Keeps the entry condition connected to the following command.
verses.before: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
verses.after: “Tell the Israelites: When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
verses.tsw_comparator: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan,

verses.rationale: States the unintentional-killing qualification without replacing it with innocence before adjudication.
verses.before: you will designate cities for yourselves to be cities of refuge, so that a manslayer who kills a person unintentionally may flee there.
verses.after: designate towns as places of refuge for yourselves, where someone who has killed a person unintentionally can flee.
verses.tsw_comparator: you shall designate cities for yourselves to be cities of refuge, so that a manslayer who kills a person unintentionally may flee there.

verses.rationale: Preserves protection pending communal judgment and the avenger role.
verses.before: The cities will be for you as refuge from the avenger, so that the manslayer may not die until standing before the congregation for judgment.
verses.after: They will be places of refuge from the avenger, so that the killer does not die before standing trial before the community.
verses.tsw_comparator: The cities shall be for you as refuge from the avenger, so that the manslayer may not die until standing before the congregation for judgment.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated six-town requirement.
verses.before: The cities that you give will be six cities of refuge for you.
verses.after: The towns you set aside will be six refuge towns.
verses.tsw_comparator: The cities that you give shall be six cities of refuge for you.

verses.rationale: Retains the equal east-west distribution without merging the eastern allotments into Canaan.
verses.before: You will give three cities beyond the Jordan and three cities in the land of Canaan; they will be cities of refuge.
verses.after: Set aside three towns on this side of the Jordan and three in the land of Canaan. They will be refuge towns.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall give three cities beyond the Jordan and three cities in the land of Canaan; they shall be cities of refuge.

verses.rationale: Preserves both outsider terms and the same refuge provision for all named groups.
verses.before: These six cities will be for refuge for the Israelites, the resident alien, and the sojourner among them, so that anyone who kills a person unintentionally may flee there.
verses.after: These six towns will be a refuge for the Israelites and for the foreigner and settler among them, so that anyone who kills a person unintentionally may flee there.
verses.tsw_comparator: These six cities shall be for refuge for the Israelites, the resident alien, and the sojourner among them, so that anyone who kills a person unintentionally may flee there.

verses.rationale: Keeps the lethal iron-object case and explicit capital consequence.
verses.before: “But if someone strikes another with an iron object so that the person dies, that one is a murderer; the murderer will surely be put to death.
verses.after: But if someone strikes a person with an iron object and the person dies, the killer is a murderer. The murderer must be put to death.
verses.tsw_comparator: “But if someone strikes another with an iron object so that the person dies, that one is a murderer; the murderer shall surely be put to death.

verses.rationale: Preserves the stone’s lethal capacity and repeated legal conclusion.
verses.before: If someone strikes another with a stone in the hand capable of causing death, and the person dies, that one is a murderer; the murderer will surely be put to death.
verses.after: If someone strikes a person with a stone held in the hand, one capable of killing, and the person dies, the killer is a murderer. The murderer must be put to death.
verses.tsw_comparator: If someone strikes another with a stone in the hand capable of causing death, and the person dies, that one is a murderer; the murderer shall surely be put to death.

verses.rationale: Keeps the separate wooden-object case and its repeated penalty rather than summarizing the series.
verses.before: Or if someone strikes another with a wooden object in the hand capable of causing death, and the person dies, that one is a murderer; the murderer will surely be put to death.
verses.after: Or if someone strikes a person with a wooden object held in the hand, one capable of killing, and the person dies, the killer is a murderer. The murderer must be put to death.
verses.tsw_comparator: Or if someone strikes another with a wooden object in the hand capable of causing death, and the person dies, that one is a murderer; the murderer shall surely be put to death.

verses.rationale: Retains the avenger’s stated agency and male role while notes connect it to the communal judgment provisions.
verses.before: The avenger of blood will put the murderer to death; when meeting the murderer, the avenger may put that person to death.
verses.after: The avenger of blood himself is to put the murderer to death. When he encounters the murderer, he is to kill him.
verses.tsw_comparator: The avenger of blood shall put the murderer to death; when meeting the murderer, the avenger may put that person to death.

verses.rationale: Preserves hatred and premeditated throwing as distinct intentional cases continuing into the next verse.
verses.before: If someone pushes another from hatred or throws something at another while lying in wait, so that the person dies,
verses.after: If someone pushes a person out of hatred, or deliberately throws something at a person and the person dies,
verses.tsw_comparator: If someone pushes another from hatred or throws something at another while lying in wait, so that the person dies,

verses.rationale: Keeps hostility, resulting death and repeated avenger instruction within the intentional-homicide sequence.
verses.before: or in hostility strikes another with the hand so that the person dies, the one who struck will surely be put to death; that one is a murderer. The avenger of blood may put the murderer to death when meeting that person.
verses.after: or strikes a person with a hand out of hostility and the person dies, the one who struck the blow must be put to death. He is a murderer; the avenger of blood is to kill the murderer when he encounters him.
verses.tsw_comparator: or in hostility strikes another with the hand so that the person dies, the one who struck shall surely be put to death; that one is a murderer. The avenger of blood may put the murderer to death when meeting that person.

verses.rationale: Retains the contrasting absence of hostility and intent in the accidental cases.
verses.before: But if someone suddenly pushes another without hostility, or throws any object without lying in wait,
verses.after: But if someone suddenly pushes a person without hostility, or throws any object at a person without intending harm,
verses.tsw_comparator: But if someone suddenly pushes another without hostility, or throws any object without lying in wait,

verses.rationale: Keeps lethal capacity, failure to see and absence of enmity or harmful purpose as cumulative case details.
verses.before: or without seeing the person drops any stone capable of causing death, and the person dies, though the killer was not an enemy and did not seek the person’s harm,
verses.after: or drops a stone capable of killing on someone without seeing them, and the person dies, though the killer was not an enemy and did not seek their harm,
verses.tsw_comparator: or without seeing the person drops any stone capable of causing death, and the person dies, though the killer was not an enemy and did not seek the person’s harm,

verses.rationale: Preserves the community’s adjudicating role between the two parties.
verses.before: then the congregation will judge between the killer and the avenger of blood according to these ordinances.
verses.after: then the community must judge between the one who struck the blow and the avenger of blood according to these rules.
verses.tsw_comparator: then the congregation shall judge between the killer and the avenger of blood according to these ordinances.

verses.rationale: Retains rescue and compulsory residence, with release tied to the specifically anointed high priest’s death.
verses.before: The congregation will rescue the manslayer from the hand of the avenger of blood and return the manslayer to the city of refuge to which that person fled. The manslayer will live there until the death of the high priest who was anointed with the holy oil.
verses.after: The community must rescue the killer from the avenger of blood and return the killer to the refuge town where they fled. The killer must stay there until the death of the high priest who was anointed with the holy oil.
verses.tsw_comparator: The congregation shall rescue the manslayer from the hand of the avenger of blood and return the manslayer to the city of refuge to which that person fled. The manslayer shall live there until the death of the high priest who was anointed with the holy oil.

verses.rationale: Keeps departure beyond the refuge boundary as the condition for the next rule.
verses.before: But if the manslayer at any time goes beyond the boundary of the city of refuge to which the person fled,
verses.after: But if the killer goes outside the boundary of the refuge town where they fled,
verses.tsw_comparator: But if the manslayer at any time goes beyond the boundary of the city of refuge to which the person fled,

verses.rationale: Preserves the exemption from bloodguilt without describing the killing as accidental or imposing a modern legal category.
verses.before: and the avenger of blood finds the person outside the boundary of the city of refuge and kills the manslayer, the avenger of blood will not be guilty of bloodshed,
verses.after: and the avenger of blood finds the killer outside that boundary and kills them, the avenger bears no bloodguilt.
verses.tsw_comparator: and the avenger of blood finds the person outside the boundary of the city of refuge and kills the manslayer, the avenger of blood shall not be guilty of bloodshed,

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated residence limit and restoration to the person’s own landholding.
verses.before: because the manslayer should have remained in the city of refuge until the death of the high priest. After the death of the high priest, the manslayer may return to the land of the possession.
verses.after: The killer must stay in the refuge town until the high priest dies. After the high priest’s death, the killer may return to the land they hold.
verses.tsw_comparator: because the manslayer should have remained in the city of refuge until the death of the high priest. After the death of the high priest, the manslayer may return to the land of the possession.

verses.rationale: Keeps enduring generational and settlement scope.
verses.before: These things will be for you a statute of justice throughout your generations in all your dwelling places.
verses.after: These rules will remain binding on you through your generations, wherever you live.
verses.tsw_comparator: These things shall be for you a statute of justice throughout your generations in all your dwelling places.

verses.rationale: Preserves plural witnesses and the explicit prohibition on capital conviction by one witness, without adding a stated number absent here. Consistency self-check: Moves the killing into the subject clause so the testimony phrase attaches clearly to the death sentence, preserving the intentional-homicide context, plural witnesses and prohibition on a single witness.
verses.before: “Whoever kills a person, the murderer will be put to death on the testimony of witnesses, but one witness will not testify against a person so that the person dies.
verses.after: A person who commits murder is to be put to death on the testimony of witnesses. But a single witness cannot testify against someone to have that person put to death.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Whoever kills a person, the murderer shall be put to death on the testimony of witnesses, but one witness shall not testify against a person so that the person dies.

consistency_revisions.rationale: Moves the killing into the subject clause so the testimony phrase attaches clearly to the death sentence, preserving the intentional-homicide context, plural witnesses and prohibition on a single witness.

verses.rationale: Keeps the no-ransom rule and its separate emphatic death requirement.
verses.before: You will accept no ransom for the life of a murderer who is guilty of death; that person will surely be put to death.
verses.after: Do not accept a ransom for the life of a murderer who deserves to die. The murderer must be put to death.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall accept no ransom for the life of a murderer who is guilty of death; that person shall surely be put to death.

verses.rationale: Retains the distinct prohibition on buying early release from refuge residence.
verses.before: You will accept no ransom for one who has fled to a city of refuge to allow that person to return and live in the land before the death of the priest.
verses.after: And do not accept a ransom for someone who has fled to a refuge town, allowing them to return and live on their land before the priest dies.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall accept no ransom for one who has fled to a city of refuge to allow that person to return and live in the land before the death of the priest.

verses.rationale: Preserves the land-blood-atonement logic and severe stated exception without substituting an explanatory doctrine.
verses.before: You will not pollute the land in which you live, for blood pollutes the land, and no atonement can be made for the land for the blood shed upon it except by the blood of the one who shed it.
verses.after: Do not pollute the land where you are, for blood pollutes the land. No atonement can be made for the land for blood shed on it except by the blood of the one who shed it.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not pollute the land in which you live, for blood pollutes the land, and no atonement can be made for the land for the blood shed upon it except by the blood of the one who shed it.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated divine dwelling connection between land and people.
verses.before: You will not defile the land in which you live, in whose midst I dwell, for I, the LORD, dwell among the Israelites.”
verses.after: Do not defile the land where you live, where I dwell, for I, the LORD, dwell among the Israelites.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not defile the land in which you live, in whose midst I dwell, for I, the LORD, dwell in the midst of the Israelites.”

verses.rationale: Unfolds the genealogy and two sets of family heads without losing the line through Joseph.
verses.before: The heads of the ancestral houses of the clan of the descendants of Gilead son of Machir, son of Manasseh, from the clans of the descendants of Joseph, came near and spoke before Moses and before the leaders, the heads of the ancestral houses of the Israelites.
verses.after: The heads of the ancestral houses in the clan of Gilead son of Machir, son of Manasseh, from the clans of Joseph’s descendants, came forward. They spoke before Moses and the leaders, the heads of the Israelites’ ancestral houses.
verses.tsw_comparator: The heads of the ancestral houses of the clan of the descendants of Gilead son of Machir, son of Manasseh, from the clans of the descendants of Joseph, came near and spoke before Moses and before the leaders, the heads of the ancestral houses of the Israelites.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes address to Moses from the divine name and preserves both commands behind the petition.
verses.before: They said, “The LORD commanded my lord to give the land as inheritance by lot to the Israelites, and my lord was commanded by the LORD to give the inheritance of Zelophehad our brother to his daughters.
verses.after: They said, “The LORD commanded my lord to give the Israelites the land as an inheritance by lot. My lord was also commanded by the LORD to give our brother Zelophehad’s inheritance to his daughters.
verses.tsw_comparator: They said, “The LORD commanded my lord to give the land as inheritance by lot to the Israelites, and my lord was commanded by the LORD to give the inheritance of Zelophehad our brother to his daughters.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated subtraction argument and its clan-centered perspective.
verses.before: But if they marry men from other tribes of the Israelites, their inheritance will be taken from the inheritance of our fathers and added to the inheritance of the tribe into which they marry; so it will be taken from the lot of our inheritance.
verses.after: If they marry men from another Israelite tribe, their inheritance will be taken away from our ancestors’ inheritance and added to the inheritance of the tribe they marry into. It will be taken away from our allotted inheritance.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if they marry men from other tribes of the Israelites, their inheritance will be taken from the inheritance of our fathers and added to the inheritance of the tribe into which they marry; so it will be taken from the lot of our inheritance.

verses.rationale: Preserves the claim that Jubilee will not reverse the tribal transfer.
verses.before: And when the Jubilee comes for the Israelites, their inheritance will be added to the inheritance of the tribe into which they marry, and their inheritance will be taken from the inheritance of our ancestral tribe.”
verses.after: Even when the Israelites’ Jubilee comes, the women’s inheritance will belong to the tribe they marry into. Their inheritance will be taken away from the inheritance of our ancestral tribe.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And when the Jubilee comes for the Israelites, their inheritance will be added to the inheritance of the tribe into which they marry, and their inheritance will be taken from the inheritance of our ancestral tribe.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the divine authorization and affirmation echoing the earlier affirmation of the daughters’ claim.
verses.before: Moses commanded the Israelites according to the word of the LORD, saying, “The tribe of the descendants of Joseph speaks rightly.
verses.after: Then, at the LORD’s command, Moses instructed the Israelites: “The tribe of Joseph’s descendants is right in what it says.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses commanded the Israelites according to the word of the LORD, saying, “The tribe of the descendants of Joseph speaks rightly.

verses.rationale: Preserves both the women’s choice and its explicit ancestral-tribal restriction.
verses.before: This is the thing that the LORD commands concerning the daughters of Zelophehad: Let them marry whomever is good in their eyes, only they will marry within a clan of their ancestral tribe.
verses.after: This is what the LORD commands concerning Zelophehad’s daughters: They may marry whomever they think best, but only within a clan of their father’s tribe.
verses.tsw_comparator: This is the thing that the LORD commands concerning the daughters of Zelophehad: Let them marry whomever is good in their eyes, only they shall marry within a clan of their ancestral tribe.

verses.rationale: Retains the individual and tribal dimensions of the no-transfer principle.
verses.before: No inheritance of the Israelites will pass from tribe to tribe, for every Israelite will hold to the inheritance of their ancestral tribe.
verses.after: An inheritance must not pass from tribe to tribe among the Israelites. Each Israelite must hold on to the inheritance of their ancestral tribe.
verses.tsw_comparator: No inheritance of the Israelites shall pass from tribe to tribe, for every Israelite shall hold to the inheritance of their ancestral tribe.

verses.rationale: Limits the marriage rule to daughters who inherit, not all women or every marriage.
verses.before: Every daughter who possesses an inheritance in any tribe of the Israelites will become the wife of someone from a clan of her father’s tribe, so that every Israelite may possess the inheritance of their ancestors.
verses.after: Every daughter who inherits land in an Israelite tribe must marry someone from a clan of her father’s tribe, so that each Israelite may retain their ancestral inheritance.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every daughter who possesses an inheritance in any tribe of the Israelites shall become the wife of someone from a clan of her father’s tribe, so that every Israelite may possess the inheritance of their ancestors.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated no-transfer conclusion rather than compressing the legal emphasis.
verses.before: No inheritance will pass from one tribe to another, for each of the tribes of the Israelites will hold to its own inheritance.”
verses.after: No inheritance may pass from one tribe to another. Each Israelite tribe must hold on to its own inheritance.”
verses.tsw_comparator: No inheritance shall pass from one tribe to another, for each of the tribes of the Israelites shall hold to its own inheritance.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the women as the actors fulfilling the instruction.
verses.before: Just as the LORD commanded Moses, so the daughters of Zelophehad did.
verses.after: Zelophehad’s daughters did as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: Just as the LORD commanded Moses, so the daughters of Zelophehad did.

verses.rationale: Preserves this verse’s distinct name order and exact paternal-cousin relationship.
verses.before: Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah, the daughters of Zelophehad, married sons of their father’s brothers.
verses.after: Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah and Noah, Zelophehad’s daughters, married sons of their father’s brothers.
verses.tsw_comparator: Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah, the daughters of Zelophehad, married sons of their father’s brothers.

verses.rationale: Retains the family line and the resulting retention of the women’s inheritance.
verses.before: They married within the clans of the descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph, and their inheritance remained with the tribe of their father’s clan.
verses.after: They married within the clans of Manasseh son of Joseph, and their inheritance remained with the tribe of their father’s clan.
verses.tsw_comparator: They married within the clans of the descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph, and their inheritance remained with the tribe of their father’s clan.

verses.rationale: Preserves the book’s closing command formula, mediation through Moses and repeated final location.
verses.before: These are the commandments and the ordinances that the LORD commanded through Moses to the Israelites in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho.
verses.after: These are the commands and rulings that the LORD gave the Israelites through Moses on the plains of Moab, by the Jordan across from Jericho.
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the commandments and the ordinances that the LORD commanded through Moses to the Israelites in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho.
